summary: Front page, Vol. XI No. 45. Main story is election gossip on Mercer County races. Target story 'R. Henri Herbert's Attack' reports that R. Henri Herbert of Trenton circulated a letter urging Black voters in Monmouth County to help defeat 'Founder' James A. Bradley, candidate for state senator, over his order barring Black waiters from his Asbury Park band pavilion the prior summer. Rest of page covers a Princeton football win, a new school gift, hospital news, an Arkansas train robbery, and local Trenton items (potteries, courts, a burglary).

people.name: R. Henri Herbert
people.role: Trenton resident who wrote and circulated a public letter urging Black voters to oppose James A. 'Founder' Bradley

people.name: James A. 'Founder' Bradley
people.role: Candidate for state senator from Monmouth County, developer of Asbury Park; target of Herbert's letter over his ban on Black waiters at his band pavilion

people.name: Frank A. Magowan
people.role: Quoted on improving Trenton rubber mill and pottery business

people.name: John G. Walker
people.role: Trenton man charged with adultery alongside Mrs. Ann Bailey

incidents.what: R. Henri Herbert issued a public letter urging Black voters in Monmouth County to defeat Bradley's state senate candidacy over the Asbury Park pavilion ban
Bradley issued an order forbidding Black waiters from visiting his Asbury Park band pavilion, the grievance cited by Herbert
Masked robbers held up an Arkansas Express mail train near Little Rock, killing the conductor

connections: Herbert's letter is an early documented instance of a Black Trentonian organizing Black voters as a bloc against a NJ political figure, relevant background for the later Black press advocacy tradition in Trenton
